title: JmapBackend::query_objects/query_changes 8-arg/9-arg positional surface forces breaks on every new RFC param
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:870-898 — JmapBackend exposes:

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn query_objects<O: QueryObject + Send + Sync>(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        filter: Option<&O::Filter>,
        sort: Option<&[O::Comparator]>,
        limit: Option<u64>,
        position: i64,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<QueryResult, Self::Error>> + Send;

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn query_changes<O: QueryObject + Send + Sync>(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        since_query_state: &jmap_types::State,
        filter: Option<&O::Filter>,
        sort: Option<&[O::Comparator]>,
        max_changes: Option<u64>,
        up_to_id: Option<&jmap_types::Id>,
        collapse_threads: bool,
    ) -> impl Future<...> + Send;

Eight and nine positional arguments respectively, each suppressed
with `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`. Clippy's lint is the
correct signal — RFC 8620 §5.5 / §5.6 do not promise the parameter
list will stay this size. New extensions / errata add params:

- RFC 8620 §5.5 itself has `anchor`, `anchorOffset` that are
  currently NOT in the trait signature. (handle_query ignores
  them; that's a separate finding, but if jmap-mail-server ever
  needs anchor support, the trait method must grow.)
- RFC 8621 §5.5 (Email/query) adds `addressbookId`, group-by
  fields, etc.
- Future ietf-jmap-* drafts (metadata, sharing, calendars) add
  per-extension query args.

What callers cannot depend on:

1. That a new RFC param can be added non-breakingly. Adding
   `anchor: Option<&Id>` to query_objects means EVERY downstream
   backend trait inheriting JmapBackend (MailBackend, ChatBackend,
   etc., currently 8 in the workspace) needs its query_objects
   impl updated. The kit ships a non-breaking trait extension
   pattern via default methods, but only if the new method has a
   sensible default. Query method new params don't have sensible
   defaults — backends MUST honor them or return a fake-correct
   answer.

2. That backend impls do not rewrite the whole signature on
   every additive change. The kit's current shape forces every
   sibling crate to do positional-arg migration in lockstep.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is:

- Workspace propagation cost compounds: every additive RFC param
  becomes a workspace-wide breaking sweep + a major-version bump.
- The trait's "additive evolution path" — the workspace AGENTS.md
  promise that "new variants on #[non_exhaustive] enums and new
  methods on traits with default impls are the additive shape" —
  doesn't apply to query_objects because the new method signature
  WOULD be a non-defaulted variant.

Resolution path:

Convert the positional args to a #[non_exhaustive] struct:

    #[non_exhaustive]
    pub struct QueryArgs<'a, O: QueryObject> {
        pub filter: Option<&'a O::Filter>,
        pub sort: Option<&'a [O::Comparator]>,
        pub limit: Option<u64>,
        pub position: i64,
        // future RFC params land here non-breakingly
    }
    fn query_objects<O: QueryObject + Send + Sync>(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        args: QueryArgs<'_, O>,
    ) -> impl Future<...>;

Now adding `anchor: Option<&'a Id>` to QueryArgs is a non-breaking
field addition. Backend impls match on `args.filter`, `args.sort`,
etc.; they default to None / 0 for unrecognised fields without
forced migration.

The propagation pass to land this is hard (8 backend crates) but
finite and one-time. The propagation pass to NOT land this is
unbounded — every future query param triggers another one.

The kit's first major bump (which is upcoming per the
canonical-templates section in workspace AGENTS.md) is the right
time to make this change.
close_reason: triage 2026-10-22 (already_fixed, skeptic-confirmed): Commit f9b9021f 'feat(server)!: params structs for query backends'. crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:406-407 adds #[non_exhaustive] pub struct QueryParams<'a, O>. query_objects takes `params: QueryParams<'_, O>` (backend.rs:823-828) and query_changes takes `QueryChangesParams<'_, O>` (backend.rs:834-841). | check: crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:406-407 defines #[non_exhaustive] pub struct QueryParams with filter, sort, limit, position, anchor and anchorOffset. Line 519-520 defines #[non_exhaustive] QueryChangesParams. query_objects (823-828) takes (caller, account_id, params: QueryParams) and query_changes
